brand_002:n1.prompt:
You are helping me generate AI-created logo images for my brand. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) my brand name, (2) a short description of my brand's tone/industry (e.g., playful fintech, minimalist wellness), (3) any preferred colors, styles, or symbols, and (4) how many logo concepts I want (default to 4-6 if I don't specify).

Using OpenAI's image generation API (DALL-E) with my configured credentials, generate the requested number of distinct logo concepts based on the brand details I provide. Write clear prompts that specify: the brand name (if it should appear as text in the logo), a clean vector/flat-icon style suitable for a logo, transparent or white background, and the tone/colors I specified. Generate a few style variations (e.g., wordmark, icon-only, combination mark) if I haven't specified a single style.

Save each generated image locally or to my configured storage with a clear filename convention (e.g., brandname_logo_01.png, brandname_logo_02.png, etc.) so they can be reviewed and compared later.

Done looks like: a set of generated logo image files saved and accessible, covering the number of concepts and style variations requested, each reasonably matching the brand description I gave.

Report back to me with: the list of saved filenames/paths, a brief description of what each logo depicts (style, colors, layout), and any notes on prompts that produced weaker results so I can decide whether to regenerate before moving to the next step (storing and setting a primary logo).

brand_002:n2.prompt:
You are helping me finish branding step brand_002:n2 — set the primary logo among the AI-generated logo images we already created and stored. Before acting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already clear: (1) the brand name/project this logo belongs to, (2) where the generated logo image files currently live (e.g., a specific folder path, cloud storage bucket, CMS media library, or database table), (3) how many candidate logos exist and any naming/versioning convention already in use, and (4) any selection criteria I want applied (e.g., preferred style, color, file format, or a specific filename I already like).

Once you have this, do the following: list the available logo candidates from the location I gave you, confirm which one I want as primary (if I haven't picked one, present the options with brief descriptions and ask me to choose — do not choose for me), then mark that file as the primary logo using whatever mechanism the storage system supports — this could mean renaming/copying it to a canonical filename (e.g., 'logo-primary.png'), setting a metadata flag or database field, or updating a manifest/config file that other tools reference. Make sure any other systems that reference 'the logo' (site header config, brand style guide doc, README) point to this same file if you have access to update them.

When done, report back: which logo file was set as primary, the exact location/identifier now marking it as primary, and any files or references you updated. If you could not determine where to write the 'primary' designation, tell me exactly what information you still need.
